articles.desc: Removing a single amino acid can determine whether new proteins assemble into stable complexes within mitochondria. Without it, numerous protein complexes lose their stability, according to a study led by Dr. Nora Vögtle of Heidelberg University and Dr. Pitter Huesgen of the University of Freiburg. articles.desc: Die Frau wollte den Erkenntnissen zufolge auf eine Bundesstraße einbiegen - und übersah einen Sattelzug. Es kam zur Kollision. Der Unfall passierte am frühen Abend in Falkenberg (Landkreis Rottal-Inn), als die Fahrerin auf die B20 einbiegen wollte, wie die Polizei mitteilte. Sie habe dabei einen vorfahrtsberechtigten Sattelzug übersehen, der in Richtung Eggenfelden fuhr. articles.title: Goldene Jahreszeit: Reiseziele für einen farbenprächtigen Herbst
articles.desc: Der Herbst verzaubert mit bunten Blättern und Weinlese. Diese fünf Ziele von Südtirol bis Japan zeigen die schönste Seite der Jahreszeit. articles.desc: We are continuously sending information to each other, transmitting zeros and ones through a giant network of connected computers and devices. The motivation is not just scientific curiosity. Qubits can be a 0, a 1 or any superposition of the two. They can also become entangled, showing a degree of correlation that is out of reach for classical bits.

articles.title: US-India satellite captures time-lapse video of volcanic eruption
articles.desc: Like tendrils on a vine, lava spreads out from the northern crater of Krasheninnikov, a volcano pair on the Pacific coast of Russia's Kamchatka Peninsula. On July 30, 2025, an 8.8-magnitude earthquake struck in the nearby ocean, apparently jolting one of the two volcanoes awake. A few days later, for the first time in nearly five centuries, Krasheninnikov started erupting. Since then, the northern volcano has been spilling a steady, eastward-flowing field of molten rock and debris, and the NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar (NISAR) mission has been tracking the changes in the landscape.

articles.title: Short peptides assemble into honeycomb fibers that hold water in tiny parallel channels
articles.desc: Honeycomb-shaped structures are familiar from beehives. Researchers have now designed molecules that self-assemble into a similar pattern on a scale far too small to see with the naked eye. These molecules are peptides: short chains of amino acids, the building blocks of proteins. Each peptide consists of only nine amino acids. Many identical copies assemble into tiny fibers with a honeycomb-like interior filled with water.
